item.title: Merchant Finance partners with Taveuni Rugby Union
item.description: MERCHANT Finance Limited is proud to support Taveuni Rugby Union as the Official Naming Rights Partner for the Union’s remaining five home games in the 2026 Skipper Cup competition. The partnership reflects Merchant Finance’s commitment to community development, grassroots sport and strengthening its presence in Taveuni, where the company has a branch.
item.content:encoded:
MERCHANT Finance Limited is proud to support Taveuni Rugby Union as the Official Naming Rights Partner for the Union’s remaining five home games in the 2026 Skipper Cup competition.

The partnership reflects Merchant Finance’s commitment to community development, grassroots sport and strengthening its presence in Taveuni, where the company has a branch.

Merchant Finance will support the Union in hosting its remaining home fixtures and encouraging player participation throughout the season. The partnership will also provide opportunities for greater community engagement through match-day activities and promotional initiatives.

Merchant Finance CEO, Veilawa Rereiwasaliwa, said the company was proud to support Taveuni as the only Northern team competing in the 2026 Skipper Cup and looked forward to developing the partnership over the coming years.

Taveuni Rugby Union Vice President, Iowane Gade, welcomed the sponsorship, noting that it will make a significant contribution to the successful completion of the Union’s 2026 campaign and benefit players, supporters and the wider community.

The partnership highlights a shared commitment to community development, youth engagement and the continued growth of rugby in Taveuni.

item.title: Sponsor boost for Navua
item.description: NAVUA FC has received a major boost ahead of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants tournament, with Blue Gas coming on board as the team’s major sponsor. Navua FC will march into the tournament as Blue Gas Navua, with the sponsorship providing added support as the side prepares to compete against the best teams in the country.
item.content:encoded:
NAVUA FC has received a major boost ahead of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants tournament, with Blue Gas coming on board as the team’s major sponsor.

Navua FC will march into the tournament as Blue Gas Navua, with the sponsorship providing added support as the side prepares to compete against the best teams in the country.

The 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants kicks off today at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

Navua FC head coach Roderick Singh acknowledged Blue Gas for supporting the team and said the players would repay the sponsor through their performances on the field.

“Thank you for coming in and being our sponsors. The team will do their uttermost best and perform at their best.

“We will make sure to give enough mileage and make sure the Blue Gas name goes up as the team progresses.

“This time, we want to thank you,” Singh said.

Singh said the sponsorship meant a lot to the team and had added motivation to their preparations for the tournament.

“Blue Gas support means a lot to us and we thank them for coming on board and supporting us. We will do our best,” he said.

He said the team had been preparing well and understood the challenge ahead.

“Our preparation has been going well. Our mentality is to prepare well because every game is going to be a challenge and every game will be tough.

“We need to control ball possession and make sure we play according to our game plan,” Singh added.

Singh said the team would take each match as it came and remain focused throughout the tournament.

He said the players were aware of the expectations and would look to make the most of the opportunity provided by the tournament.

With Blue Gas now backing the side, Navua FC will be hoping to make a strong start to their Extra BOG campaign today at Govind Park.

item.title: Franklin impresses on international debut
item.description: NICHOLAS Franklin is quickly finding his feet with the Junior Bula Boys after making a strong start to his international campaign in Samoa. The 18-year-old midfielder was named player of the match after helping Fiji defeat Vanuatu 7-2 in its opening match of the OFC under-19 Men’s Championship.
item.content:encoded:
NICHOLAS Franklin is quickly finding his feet with the Junior Bula Boys after making a strong start to his international campaign in Samoa.

The 18-year-old midfielder was named player of the match after helping Fiji defeat Vanuatu 7-2 in its opening match of the OFC under-19 Men’s Championship.

Franklin was raised in Brisbane, Australia, but has a strong connection to Fiji through his mother who is from Suva.

His father is Irish, giving the 18-year-old midfielder Fijian and Irish Heritage.

He developed his football in Brisbane and currently plays for Eastern Suburbs, before earning his opportunity with the Junior Bula Boys.

Representing Fiji has therefore been an opportunity for him to combine his football ambitions with his family connection.

“I live in Australia, but my mum is from Fiji, and being able to represent her heritage is really special for our family, for the ones watching at home, and for my mum and dad here as well.”

His introduction to the team has proved fruitful, with Franklin scoring Fiji’s final goal in stoppage time to complete a convincing opening victory.

However, the midfielder said the performance was the result of the understanding built within the squad during their preparation.

“It’s been a long journey so far. The boys had a four-week camp in Fiji, being away from our families and everything. It’s been long, but we’ve had each other and it showed in that game,” Franklin said.

Franklin was surprised to receive the individual award, believing several of his teammates were equally deserving after Fiji’s seven-goal performance.

“It’s good to get player of the match. Honestly, I didn’t think I was going to get it. A lot of the boys in our team put in a good shift and a few of the definitely deserved it.”

His inclusion has also added dimension to a squad made up pf players from Fiji and overseas.

Franklin now turns his attention to Fiji’s next assignment against New Zealand.

He expects the match to provide a far greater test but believes the Junior Bula Boys can take confidence from their opening performance.

“Everyone knows it’s going to be a big game for us. They’re a good team, so we’ve just got to go in there with our heads down and hopefully put in a good result for us and get the job done.”

For Franklin, his first tournament appearance has already provided an encouraging start, but the midfielder knows the bigger challenge is still ahead.

item.title: Bulikula name 42 for World Cup
item.description: FIJI National Rugby League has named a 42-member extended Bulikula squad for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup in Australia, blending local talent with a strong Australian-based contingent. Fifteen players, more than a third of the squad, are drawn straight from the domestic competition at home, among them USP Raiders pair Naomi Tegu and Reape Diege Matai and Police Sharks trio Temalesi Bui Natuitub
item.content:encoded:
FIJI National Rugby League has named a 42-member extended Bulikula squad for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup in Australia, blending local talent with a strong Australian-based contingent.

Fifteen players, more than a third of the squad, are drawn straight from the domestic competition at home, among them USP Raiders pair Naomi Tegu and Reape Diege Matai and Police Sharks trio Temalesi Bui Natuituba, Adi Soakula and Laisa Takayawa.

The remaining 27 come from three Australian competitions.

Fourteen ply their trade in the National Rugby League Women’s Premiership (NRLW), including Cronulla Sharks pair Cassie Staples and Talei Holmes and Canberra Raiders duo Isabella Waterman and Sereana Naitokatoka.

Four are drawn from the New South Wales Rugby League (NSWRL), among them Wentworthville Magpies’ Siniva Sa’anga, while nine come from the Queensland Rugby League’s BMD Premiership (QRL), including Burleigh Bears pair Teaghan Hartigan and Ebony Laing.

Twenty of the 42 were part of the 25-strong squad that sealed Fiji’s maiden World Cup berth with a 62-4 win over Nigeria in the World Series final in Brampton, Ontario, last October.

Captain Cassie Staples, who scored four tries in that final, leads the returning core alongside Talei Holmes, Latisha Smythe, Losana Lutu, Isabella Waterman, Sereana Naitokatoka and Maria Paseka.

Rise Rookie graduate Tegu, who scored in the World Series semi-final win over Canada, is also retained, a sign of the pathway from Fiji’s domestic and development ranks bearing fruit ahead of Fiji’s first-ever World Cup appearance.

Newly appointed Fiji Bulikula head coach Jone Wesele understands the magnitude of the task ahead – with so much expectation in their Rugby League World Cup debut players will need to step up for a place in the final 23.

“We are not just going there to participate we are going there to establish the Fiji Bulikua and we are going there to win,” Wesele said.

The 2026 Rugby League World Cup will be played across Australia and Papua New Guinea from October 16 till November 15.

Ba FC players and management spent time with the senior citizens as part of an initiative focused on giving back to the community and showing appreciation to the elders who helped build
item.content:encoded:
DAYAL’S Steel Ba Football Association and Ba FC management today honoured the senior citizens of Ba, seeking their blessings ahead of the 2026 Battle of the Giants tournament at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

Ba FC players and management spent time with the senior citizens as part of an initiative focused on giving back to the community and showing appreciation to the elders who helped build Ba.

The club also provided lunch for the senior citizens and distributed 100 complimentary BOG 2026 tickets valued at $20 each, covering all five days of the tournament. In addition, 100 food vouchers will be provided for each day of the tournament.

Ba FC president Praneel Dayal believes the initiative reflects Ba FC’s commitment to the wider Ba community and its belief that football is more than what happens on the field.

“Our players carry the hopes of Ba onto the field, but today they stood before our elders with humble hearts.”

The gesture was about respect, gratitude, community and giving back to those who have contributed to the development of Ba over the years.

“We Play for Ba. We Serve Ba. We Honour Ba.

item.title: Ultra race starts in Ra
item.description: A GRUELLING 68km journey through Ra will today mark the beginning of what organisers hope will become one of Fiji’s biggest endurance challenges, with 17 ultra runners taking part in the inaugural Mangroves to Mountains race. Over two days, the runners will cover 68km through mangroves, farmland, river crossings and mountainous terrain, tackling a route that organisers hope will one day form part
item.content:encoded:
A GRUELLING 68km journey through Ra will today mark the beginning of what organisers hope will become one of Fiji’s biggest endurance challenges, with 17 ultra runners taking part in the inaugural Mangroves to Mountains race.

Over two days, the runners will cover 68km through mangroves, farmland, river crossings and mountainous terrain, tackling a route that organisers hope will one day form part of a much larger coast-to-coast challenge across Viti Levu.

The race begins at Nanumi Au Eco Village, where runners gathered yesterday for final preparations before setting off on the first 30km stage to Nananu Village.

The opening day takes competitors beneath the Nakauvadra ridge before sending them into a steep climb through Yaqara farmland. After an overnight stop in Nananu, the runners will face an even tougher 38km journey tomorrow, finishing at Savulelele Waterfall near Nabalesere.

For organisers, however, the inaugural event is about much more than who reaches the finish line first.

The race is being staged by Talanoa Treks as a test event for a proposed five-day coast-to-coast ultramarathon across Viti Levu in 2027.

Event co-ordinator Marita Manley said the race would challenge competitors physically and mentally while also testing the route and logistics for the larger event planned for next year.

“This is a test event for a larger event next year, and we’re really thankful for the time and commitment the community in Ra has put into this event,” Manley said.

“This course is not about competing with other runners – it is a competition against the terrain and yourself.”

The event has brought together eight communities along the route, with Nanumi Au Eco Village, Nabalesere Co-operative, Yaqara Pastoral Company, Rakiraki Town Council, Fiji Pine and the iTaukei Trust Fund Board also involved.

Warm and humid conditions are expected to add another layer to the challenge, with runners advised to carefully manage their pace and use stream crossings along the route to cool down.

While only 17 runners will line up for this inaugural journey, organisers hope the event will lay the groundwork for something far bigger.

If successful, the Mangroves to Mountains race could become the first step towards bringing endurance athletes from around the world to Fiji to take on a five-day journey from coast to coast.

For now, though, the challenge is simple: 68km of Ra’s rugged landscape stand between the runners and the finish line.

item.title: Suvavou reclaim Tui Suva trophy
item.description: SUVAVOU reclaimed the Tui Suva Trophy after two years, defeating Vatuwaqa 16-12 at Albert Park, Suva, as part of the week-long Hibiscus Festival celebrations. Coach Jope Qalia Vutikalulu praised his players for their commitment and hard work in the lead-up to the match.
item.content:encoded:
SUVAVOU reclaimed the Tui Suva Trophy after two years, defeating Vatuwaqa 16-12 at Albert Park, Suva, as part of the week-long Hibiscus Festival celebrations.

Coach Jope Qalia Vutikalulu praised his players for their commitment and hard work in the lead-up to the match.

The team trained twice a day over the past three weeks, with the coach saying that preparation played an important role in their performance.

“I want to thank the boys for their hard work over these three weeks, for the big training we do in the evening and the morning,” Vutikalulu said.

He said the match also provided an opportunity for the players to test themselves and continue developing their skills.

“The boys tried to build up their level of rugby to come into the level of A, so they can enter a big competition like Skipper Cup or go right to the Drua,” he said.

Vutikalulu said the club would continue working with the players through regular weekend rugby, with the aim of developing them for higher-level competitions.

The coach also acknowledged the strong support from the communities who attended the match.

“I thank everyone who attended this game today, a very important game, a very interesting game,” he said.

“I thank Kubuna, Burebasaga and Tovata, they came in numbers to support this good game.”

The 16-12 victory saw Suvavou take the Tui Suva Trophy back after a two-year absence, giving the side a fitting celebration during the Hibiscus Festival.
